answer.reason: Jerusalem is a great city, and a few defining events of its story are plainly stated in the verses: its capture by Judah, David's taking of it, and its burning by the Chaldeans.

clauses.english: was taken by the children of Judah, smitten with the sword and set on fire
clauses.quote: the children of Judah had fought against Jerusalem, and had taken it

clauses.english: was taken by David from the Jebusites and became the city of David
clauses.quote: Nevertheless David took the strong hold of Zion: the same is the city of David.

clauses.english: was besieged by Nebuchadnezzar, and its temple, houses and walls were burned and broken down
clauses.quote: And he burnt the house of the LORD, and the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem

doubts: Marked verses naming Salem (GEN 14:18, HEB 7:1-2) concern Melchizedek's Salem; the verses here do not identify it with Jerusalem, so they were left out.
Jebus/Jebusite verses (JOS 15:63, JDG 1:21, JDG 19:10) were left out because the clauses chosen rest on stronger events.
